newsitem.title: UK: Abbey National bounces after trade update.
newsitem.headline: Abbey National bounces after trade update.

text.p: Abbey National shares recovered on Wednesday as weakness on the back of the bank's trading statement Tuesday was thought to be overdone, traders said.
"The statement was better than expected but everybody had worked themselves up over it because Abbey has been a pretty awful performer over the last quarter," said one market source.
The shares were up 6p to 606-1/2p by 1037 GMT, as investors took heart from forecasts that transactions and lending figures will reach a new five-year high next year.
"On the plus side they raised their estimates for the mortgage market's total growth," said the market source.
Analysts said the initial setback in the share-price arose as the statement highlighted the bank's loss of market share in new mortgages by refusing to quantify it.
SBC Warburg cut their current year forecasts by 60 million, down to 1,168 million stg and shaved 20 million off their 1997 forecast. But the broker held its "add" recommendation.
The Financial Times said on Wednesday that Abbey's share of new mortages could be around six percent, well below the 15 percent share of existing lending.

"The Financial Times flagged six percent this morning," said one leading industry analyst. "But I don't think it's as much as this considering what the competition has been like in the mortgage market recently."
